text:
ops-bot: INFO: automated firmware rollout completed to us-central racks 7-10 at 04:02 UTC. Telemetry spike: OOB timeouts + firmware-state mismatches.

leo: seeing a weird spike in GPU allocation failures after the rollout. Multiple nodes reporting UEFI policy errors during PXE. capacity impacted ~9% (21/240 GPUs).

priya: which firmware image was pushed? vendor-bot: image id `bmc-usw-2026-03-20-b` (sha256: ab12...).

vendor-bot: NOTE: release notes indicate "secure-boot policy enforcement improvements" as part of this build.

meera: repro from edge-provisioner: ```
2026-03-21T04:05:12Z provisioner ERROR node=usc-rack08-03: pxeboot: uefi policy mismatch (required signed image)
2026-03-21T04:05:13Z bmc WARN node=usc-rack08-03: rtc skew detected: 12s
2026-03-21T04:05:14Z scheduler ERROR job=job-9847: allocation failed (no compatible boot)
```

leo: rtc skew? that can break cert validation for PXE signed payloads. are BMCs changing RTC during update?

meera: yes, `ipmitool sel list` shows NTP not syncing on several hosts after firmware applied. ipmitool mc info shows `bmc-usw-2026-03-20-b` on affected hosts.

priya: mitigation ideas: 1) pause autoscale 2) fallback to unsigned-allowed image for critical jobs 3) rollback firmware on worst racks. Thoughts?

oncall-jordan: I'm grabbing console serials. Also enabling a temporary fleet flag `oob.accept_time_skew=15s` to avoid immediate sigcheck fails. That should reduce reboots.

ops-bot: playbook executed: `PATCH /infra/flags/oob.accept_time_skew` by oncall-jordan (value=15s).

leo: that may help short-term but we need permanent fix. If RTC drift persists, bootloader signature checks will keep failing. Could be BMC resetting RTC to epoch after update.

meera: found serial excerpt from usc-rack09-11: ```
Mar 21 04:03:01 BMC: firmware-init: rtc zeroing to 1970-01-01
Mar 21 04:03:02 UEFI: Certificate validation: failed (time outside cert validity)
Mar 21 04:03:03 PXE: aborting boot
```

priya: yikes. vendor needs to confirm why the fw resets RTC. Opening vendor ticket VT-4621 and attaching logs.

vendor-bot: Vendor ticket VT-4621 created referencing `bmc-usw-2026-03-20-b`. Vendor ack 04:15 UTC, assigned to firmware team.

meera: proposed immediate plan: 1) tag current build as `hold` in artifact repo 2) schedule rollback for racks 8-9 (most impacted) 3) run canary after rollback 4) add RTC sanity preflight to firmware rollout pipeline.

leo: cost/capacity note: current retry rate ~95/min, estimated hourly bill +4% if retries continue. Rollback will cause 1-2 minute reboots * 14 nodes but drastically reduce retries. I prefer rollback.

oncall-jordan: I'm starting targeted rollback on usc-rack08. Steps: annotate nodes with `maintenance=fw-rollback`, drain GPUs, flash `bmc-usw-2026-02-10-stable`, verify `date` and efivar `SecureBoot` status.

ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: provisioning autoscale paused for us-central at 04:12 UTC.

priya: while rollback runs, add a temporary allocation policy for non-critical batch jobs to use a signed-compat image that allows a 30s time-window. Update provisioning config: `fallback_image=signed-compat-v2`

meera: rollback results for usc-rack08: `efivar -l | grep SecureBoot` shows `SecureBoot=0` and `date` reports correct time. Canaries successful (5 allocations).

leo: rolling rollback to rack09 now. Also adding telemetry metric `bmc.rtc_offset_seconds` with alert threshold 5s.

vendor-bot: vendor response: reproduced issue internally, root cause in RTC init path when NTP not reachable during firstboot. Patch ETA 48h, recommended rollback or config change to preserve RTC across flash.

priya: action items: 1) preflight: check NTP reachability and RTC non-zero before promoting fw 2) add `bmc.rtc_offset_seconds` to fleet dashboards 3) vendor to provide signed manifest with explicit behavior 4) update runbook to include `oob.accept_time_skew` toggle.

oncall-jordan: provisioning resumed at 04:39 UTC with conservative retry backoff. Monitoring retry rate and cost.

leo: filing post-incident blameless note and scheduling follow-up in #eng-infra-incident-review tomorrow. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
